name: Nation
overview: Scripture reveals that a nation's standing before God is deeply affected by both the righteousness and sins of its people and leaders, as seen when Abimelech pleads for the preservation of a righteous nation (Genesis 20:4) and laments the great sin brought upon his kingdom (Genesis 20:9). The sin of individuals, such as Achan's trespass, can provoke God's anger against the entire nation, resulting in national adversity and defeat (Joshua 7:1, 11-12). Yet, God promises peace and protection to His people when they live righteously, assuring them that He will remove threats and grant rest in the land (Leviticus 26:6). These passages emphasize the vital connection between national holiness, divine favor, and the peace that God alone can provide.
